cf-6-036.title: The Ledger Closes
cf-6-036.text:
Silence settles over the high vaulted room like a blanket of grey wool, heavy with the weight of unreadable debts and dry parchment. The Stationmaster-General watches the dark ink settle into the grain of the page, her ancient fingers resting entirely still beside the bone-handled pen. Below your boots, the deep thrum of the engine dies away into a faint, shivering rattle as the last measure of pressure bleeds from the regulator and leaves the brass cold to the touch. There is no water rising in the dry basins, and the massive valves remain stubbornly bolted against the dust of the steppes.

You stand alone in the quiet gloom with a brass key that has lost its purpose and a furnace that will never draw another breath, while the low sky outside darkens toward an endless winter of ash and iron.
exits: Leave the silent keep by the heavy oak doors

cf-6-037.title: Cold Ash and Iron
cf-6-037.text: Outside the gallery windows, the great walled city of Cinderfall lies mute beneath a low, yellowish sky that threatens to bury the remaining rooftops in drifts of dry grit. You walk down through the narrow, unlit stairwells where the smell of stale coal smoke clings stubbornly to the stonework, past ticket-windows that will never open again and signal-boxes whose levers have rusted fast in their iron beds. No steam whistles greet the twilight, and no gangers walk the platform with their oil-lamps swinging in the gloom. The Marrowbone waits on the dead siding outside the walls, her boiler stone-cold and her fire-box choked with the grey leavings of a journey that ended just short of salvation. You fold your heavy coat against the rising wind from the steppes and set off down the track on foot, leaving the engine to rust among the weeds while the ash-storms close their grey fingers over the last road.

cf-6-038.title: The Water Rises
cf-6-038.text: A long, deep groan shakes the foundations of the ancient masonry as the massive brass valves finally turn under the leverage of your tired arms, biting through decades of green scale and dried grease with a sharp, metallic shriek. For a breathless moment nothing moves, and then a heavy, subterranean shudder runs through the stone channels beneath your boots, followed by the sudden, glorious roar of dark water leaping from the deep mountain springs into the empty reservoirs. The spray catches the dim light of the high clerestory windows, turning the drifting dust to gold as the cool, sweet scent of wet earth and living river fills the damp galleries. Down in the city below, distant shouts rise from the courtyards as the dry fountains begin to gush and the garden beds drink their fill after years of thirst. You wipe the black grease from your forehead with a soot-stained sleeve and lean against the massive wheel, listening to the music of the rushing water that has finally come home.

cf-6-039.title: Schedule and Sovereign
cf-6-039.text: The ledger remains open upon the polished walnut desk, its heavy pages ruled in neat, unrelenting columns of black and red ink that account for every ton of coal and every gallon of water left in the hills. The Rail Barons' agent nods once, a curt, small motion of a chin resting above a stiff linen collar, and reaches out to lay a heavy thumb over the brass key you have placed upon the green baize. Outside the high tall windows, the marshalling yards begin to shift with the smooth, oiled precision of a well-kept timetable as fresh locomotives back into the sidings to haul away the surplus. You receive your sealed discharge and a modest purse of minted copper, the legal price of an engine surrendered and a debt duly paid according to the rule of the line. The Marrowbone is someone else's property now, her fire drawn and her brass polished for a master who cares nothing for the ash-storms, leaving you to turn your back on the tracks and find your way into a city that runs by someone else's clock.
